interactions.summary: A student finally names the eclipse, and Jiang confirms that the eclipse is exactly why the moon cannot be hollow all the way through.

Carol reads the second version of the cavity theory, where reflected light from a deeper section should appear dimmer, and Jiang restates it as the remaining logical fallback once the hollow-moon option has been eliminated.

Carol reads Beatrice's answer that experiment can free Dante from error, Jiang turns that into a theological challenge to test rather than merely believe, and the poem's three-mirror experiment becomes Jiang's concrete proof that distance changes apparent size but not brightness, defeating the deep-cavity theory too.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Carol reading with Jiang interpretation and experimental gloss

claims.claim: Jiang confirms that the eclipse is the decisive evidence against the idea that the moon is hollow in some part all the way through.
Jiang reconstructs the remaining logical fallback as a deep-cavity model in which light reflected from farther back inside the moon should come back dimmer.
Jiang interprets Beatrice's invitation to experiment as a refusal of authoritarian belief: even a representative of God tells Dante to test the claim for himself.

Jiang says the three-mirror experiment shows that a more distant reflected image may be smaller but will match the brightness of the nearer ones, so the deep-cavity explanation of the moon's dim spots also fails.
Jiang concludes that Beatrice uses reason and experiment to refute a merely logical account of the moon, so reason here defeats its own simplistic use rather than being abandoned.

signature_moments.moment: Beatrice is recast as divine authority telling Dante not to obey blindly but to run the experiment himself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you don't have to believe me... you have the power to know the truth for yourself
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves Jiang's striking fusion of theology, freedom, and empirical verification.

signature_moments.moment: The mirror experiment becomes a kitchen-table demonstration that collapses the moon's deep-cavity theory.
signature_moments.source_phrase: although the image in the farthest glass will be of lesser size, there you will see that it must match the brightness of the rest
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's memorable hinge between poetic argument and repeatable empirical test.

signature_moments.moment: Reason is forced to expose the failure of its own first explanation.
signature_moments.source_phrase: through logic, for reason, she's able to refute your logic and reason as well
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This keeps Jiang's method from collapsing into anti-rationalism; the issue is shallow logic, not inquiry itself.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The means by which Beatrice frees Dante from error, and for Jiang a model of testing truth rather than merely submitting to authority.
Beatrice's demonstration that increased distance changes apparent size but not brightness, used to refute the dimness-by-depth theory of the moon.

chronology_notes.note: This packet completes the two-step demolition of the density theory: first the eclipse rules out hollowness, then experiment rules out the deep-cavity fallback, while Jiang stresses that truth here is approached through testing rather than deference.

uncertainty_notes.note: The poem line in the cleaned transcript remains noisy ('free you from your cabal' / 'arts course springs from experiment'), but Jiang's paraphrase makes the function unambiguous: Beatrice appeals to experiment as a path out of error.
